'''Martin Jim Aitken''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Spooner |first=N. A. |last2=Smith |first2=B. W. |last3=Sanderson |first3=D. C. W. |date=2025 |title=Martin Jim Aitken: 11 March 1922 — 13 June 2017 |url=https://doi.org/10.1098/rsbm.2025.0006 |journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society |volume=79}}</ref> (11 March 1922<ref>{{cite book|last=Ellis|first=Linda|title=Archaeological Method and Theory: An Encyclopedia|year=2000|publisher=Garland Publishing|location=New York|isbn=978-0815313052|page=10}}</ref> – 13 June 2017<ref>{{cite journal|title=Martin Aitken: A personal recollection | doi=10.1016/j.quageo.2018.09.004 |journal=Quaternary Geochronology|volume = 48| pages=145 |year = 2018| s2cid=240138096 }}</ref>) was a British [[Archaeometry|archaeometrist]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aber.ac.uk/temp-ancient-tl/issue20_1/notices_atl_20(1)_29-32.pdf|title=Jubilee Aitken - an eightieth birthday celebration|access-date=26 July 2011|archive-date=4 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181004185927/http://www.aber.ac.uk/temp-ancient-tl/issue20_1/notices_atl_20(1)_29-32.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=libraryofcongress>{{LCAuth|n84167794|M. J. Aitken|10|ue}}</ref>

==Biography==
Aitken was born in [[Stamford, Lincolnshire]], and studied physics at [[Wadham College, Oxford]]. He was a fellow of [[Linacre College, Oxford]].<ref name="obit G">{{cite news |last1=Aitken |first1=Jessica |title=Martin Aitken obituary |url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2017/aug/24/martin-aitken-obituary |access-date=18 November 2021 |work=The Guardian |date=24 August 2017 |language=en}}</ref> He was Professor of Archaeometry at the [[University of Oxford]] from 1985 until he retired in 1989.<ref name="obit G" /><ref>{{cite journal| doi=10.1111/j.1475-4754.1990.tb01076.x | volume=32|journal=Archaeometry|pages=3–6|year = 1990|last1 = Hall|first1 = E. T.| last2=Aitken | first2=M. J. | last3=Sayre | first3=E. V. | title=On the Retirement of Teddy Hall and Martin Aitken }}</ref>

Aitken organised annual meetings that became the Symposium on Archaeometry and Archaeological Prospection.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.arch.ox.ac.uk/rlaha.html|title=Research Laboratory for Archaeology & the History of Art|work=ox.ac.uk}}</ref> He had an interest in [[absolute dating]]: [[radiocarbon dating]] from 1957, [[thermoluminescence dating]] from the 1960s, and later helped develop [[optically stimulated luminescence]] as a dating method dating.<ref name="obit G" />

He died in June 2017 at the age of 95.<ref>[https://www.dansnoscoeurs.fr/martin-jim-aitken/2110971/avis Avis de décès] (in French)</ref>
